newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two brokers say to cut Japan OTC fees by 70 pct.
newsitem.headline: Two brokers say to cut Japan OTC fees by 70 pct.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets Ltd and Fukuyama Securities Co Ltd said on Wednesday they were planning to cut their brokerage fees for stocks and convertible bonds traded on Japan's over-the-counter market.
"We have not decided formally on the fee reduction, but we are pretty sure we will be able to cut transaction fees by 70 percent starting September," a Paribas spokesman said.
He said Paribas believed that Japan's over-the-counter fees were much too high and that reducing fees would encourage more investors to engage in trade.
"We halved our fee earlier this year and the response has been extremely good," he added. "A further cut should be well-received by investors."
Paribas slashed its fees by half effective from January 31, prompting other brokerages to do the same.

Fukuyama Securities, which had not rushed to join the discount trend, announced on Wednesday that it too would cut its brokerage fees by 70 percent for OTC stock, convertible bonds and warrants for transactions exceeding 10 million yen.
"We think that investors, especially large-lot investors, will benefit greatly from the move," a spokesman said.
The brokerage said it would reduce fees for transactions below five million yen by 30 percent and for those between five million and 10 million yen by 50 percent.
The reduction will be effective from July 14, the spokesman said.
